words.enDefinition: choosing which costs to collect and how to assign them to support useful decisions

examples.en: The course discussed cost system design for a print shop that handled several sizes of order.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了接多种规模订单的印刷店该如何做「成本核算系统设计」。

examples.en: The new cost system design collected setup hours separately from the time spent printing each order.
examples.zh: 新的「成本核算系统设计」把设备准备工时与每笔订单的实际印刷时间分别归集。

words.enDefinition: a report prepared for people within an organisation to show how costs were incurred or assigned

examples.en: The internal cost report showed labour and materials separately for every job that month.
examples.zh: 「内部成本报告」按当月每项作业分别列出人工和材料成本。

examples.en: We compared the internal cost report with the original estimate for the theatre scenery project.
examples.zh: 我们把「内部成本报告」与剧场布景项目的原先估算作了比较。

collocations: figures in an internal cost report

words.enDefinition: a system that accumulates and assigns costs to individual orders, jobs or batches

examples.en: The print shop used job order costing because each society requested a different set of materials.
examples.zh: 各社团要求的材料各不相同，印刷店采用「分批成本法」。

examples.en: Our lecturer used job order costing to estimate what the custom display had cost to make.
examples.zh: 讲师用「分批成本法」估算制作定制展示台花了多少钱。

words.enDefinition: a system that accumulates costs by process or department and averages them over similar units of output

examples.en: We used process costing because the workshop produced identical notebooks in a continuous series of steps.
examples.zh: 工作室连续经过一系列步骤生产相同的笔记本，我们用的是「分步成本法」。

examples.en: The class compared process costing for the standard badges with separate costing for custom orders.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了标准徽章用的「分步成本法」与定制订单单独核算的做法。

words.zhGloss: 工序与分批结合的成本法
words.enDefinition: a hybrid costing system combining job costing for some inputs with process costing for common operations
acceptedZhAnswers: 工序与分批结合的成本法

examples.en: The shoe example used operation costing because each batch used different fabric but followed identical assembly steps.
examples.zh: 示例中的鞋采用「工序与分批结合的成本法」，各批用料不同，组装步骤一致。

examples.en: Our lecturer compared operation costing with process costing for products made entirely from the same materials.
examples.zh: 讲师把「工序与分批结合的成本法」与所有产品原材料完全相同情况下用的分步成本法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a method assigning costs to a batch of identical or similar items, often to calculate the unit cost

examples.en: We applied batch costing to estimate the production cost of one notebook in the latest batch.
examples.zh: 我们用「按批核算成本」估算最新一批笔记本中一本的生产成本。

examples.en: The workbook explained batch costing using several identical kits prepared together for the course.
examples.zh: 练习册用为课程一起准备的几套相同用具讲解「按批核算成本」。

words.enDefinition: determining and assigning the cost of providing a service, often per measurable unit

examples.en: We used service costing to estimate the cost per hour of equipment support at the university.
examples.zh: 我们用「服务成本核算」估计学校每小时设备支持的成本。

examples.en: The lecturer explained how service costing differed between a repair desk and a delivery service.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了维修台和送货服务的「服务成本核算」有什么不同。

words.enDefinition: a record showing direct materials, direct labour and allocated overhead for a specific job

examples.en: The job cost sheet listed the paper used for the drama society's poster order.
examples.zh: 「作业成本单」列了话剧社海报订单所用的纸张。

examples.en: I checked the job cost sheet before comparing the budget with the cost of the finished display.
examples.zh: 我先查了「作业成本单」，再比较预算和展示台实际完工的成本。

collocations: post costs to a job cost sheet

words.enDefinition: a reference number used to identify a specific order or work assignment in a costing or tracking system

examples.en: We wrote the job number on each receipt before entering its cost on the sheet.
examples.zh: 填成本单之前，我们在每张收据上写了「作业编号」。

examples.en: The supervisor asked me to check the job number before assigning the materials to the order.
examples.zh: 主管请我先核对「作业编号」，再把材料成本记到订单上。

collocations: match a receipt to a job number

words.enDefinition: a ledger containing the detailed cost records for individual jobs

examples.en: The job ledger showed which completed orders still needed their labour costs to be entered.
examples.zh: 「作业成本明细账」显示了哪些已完工订单还需要录入人工成本。

examples.en: We used the job ledger to trace the cost of plywood back to the theatre display.
examples.zh: 我们通过「作业成本明细账」把胶合板成本追溯到了剧场展示台。

collocations: post costs to the job ledger

words.enDefinition: the process of collecting costs for later assignment to jobs, departments, activities or other objects

examples.en: During cost accumulation, we grouped the printer charges with other costs for the same job.
examples.zh: 进行「成本归集」时，我们把打印机费用和同一作业的其他成本归在一起。

examples.en: The lecturer demonstrated cost accumulation for two production departments before discussing overhead allocation in class.
examples.zh: 讲师先演示了两个生产部门怎么进行「成本归集」，然后讨论间接费用分配。

words.enDefinition: an instruction authorising the production of a specified quantity of an item or batch

examples.en: The production order authorised fifty notebooks for the department's orientation event at the end of August.
examples.zh: 「生产工单」批准为系里八月底举办的迎新活动生产五十本笔记本。

examples.en: The workshop checked the production order before cutting the materials for the next batch.
examples.zh: 工作室先核查了「生产工单」，才裁切下一批的材料。

words.enDefinition: a form requesting materials from stores and recording which work will use them

examples.en: I entered the job number on the materials requisition form before collecting the fabric.
examples.zh: 去领布料前，我在「领料单」上填了作业编号。

examples.en: The materials requisition form showed that the printing job used two different weights of paper.
examples.zh: 「领料单」显示，印刷作业用了两种不同克重的纸。

collocations: match a materials requisition form to a job

words.enDefinition: the release of materials from inventory for use in production or on a job

examples.en: The storekeeper recorded the materials issue when the paper was released for the booklet order.
examples.zh: 纸张领去制作小册子订单时，仓管员记录了这次「材料领发」。

examples.en: We matched the materials issue to the job number before assigning its cost to the order.
examples.zh: 把成本分配给订单前，我们先把「材料领发」记录与作业编号对应起来。

words.enDefinition: the return to inventory of unused materials that were previously issued to a job or department

examples.en: The unused materials return reduced the fabric cost shown on the original job sheet.
examples.zh: 「剩余材料退库」冲减了原作业单上记录的布料成本。

examples.en: We recorded an unused materials return after finding that the display needed only two sheets of card.
examples.zh: 发现展示台只需两张卡纸后，我们登记了一次「剩余材料退库」。

words.enDefinition: a document recording time spent on particular jobs or activities by a worker

examples.en: The labour time record showed how much of the afternoon was spent assembling the display stand.
examples.zh: 「人工用时记录」写明了下午有多少时间花在组装展示架上。

examples.en: We checked the labour time record before charging the work to the two orders.
examples.zh: 把人工费用计入两笔订单前，我们核对了「人工用时记录」。

collocations: hours on a labour time record

words.enDefinition: hours spent by workers on production or service work directly traceable to a cost object

examples.en: We counted the direct labour hours used to assemble each student prize pack that morning.
examples.zh: 我们统计了当天上午组装各份学生奖品包所用的「直接人工工时」。

examples.en: The workbook used direct labour hours to assign overhead in the small printing shop.
examples.zh: 练习册以「直接人工工时」为依据，分配小印刷店的间接费用。

words.enDefinition: the amount of time machines are operated, often used as a measure for assigning costs

examples.en: The workshop allocated equipment costs using machine hours recorded by the cutting department each week.
examples.zh: 工作室用切割部门每周记录的「机器工时」分配设备成本。

examples.en: I included all the machine hours the equipment spent printing the two exhibition banners.
examples.zh: 我把设备印两幅展览横幅所用的全部「机器工时」都计了进去。

words.enDefinition: an overhead or cost rate calculated per hour of machine use

examples.en: We used the machine-hour rate to calculate how much overhead to assign to each order.
examples.zh: 我们用「每机器工时费率」计算各笔订单该分到多少间接费用。

examples.en: The machine-hour rate rose when we forecast the same overhead across fewer hours of use.
examples.zh: 预计把同样的间接费用分摊到更少的使用时数后，「每机器工时费率」提高了。

words.enDefinition: a department that provides support to other departments rather than producing the organisation's main output

examples.en: The campus printing centre had a service department that maintained the equipment used for production.
examples.zh: 校园印刷中心有个「辅助服务部门」，负责维护生产使用的设备。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why a service department might share its costs across two production areas.
examples.zh: 导师解释了为什么一个「辅助服务部门」的成本会由两个生产区分摊。

words.enDefinition: an overhead rate calculated separately for a department using an allocation base appropriate to it

examples.en: The departmental overhead rate for printing used machine hours because most of its costs came from equipment.
examples.zh: 印刷部门大部分成本来自设备，所以其「部门间接费用分配率」以机器工时为依据。

examples.en: We applied a different departmental overhead rate for the finishing work on the same job.
examples.zh: 同一作业的后道加工采用了另一个「部门间接费用分配率」。

words.zhGloss: 全厂统一间接费用分配率
words.enDefinition: one overhead rate used across an entire manufacturing facility
acceptedZhAnswers: 全厂统一间接费用分配率

examples.en: The case used a plantwide overhead rate before comparing results from separate rates for two departments.
examples.zh: 案例先用「全厂统一间接费用分配率」，再比较两个部门各自采用费率算出的结果。

examples.en: We calculated the plantwide overhead rate from total estimated overhead and machine hours for the facility.
examples.zh: 我们根据工厂预估的总间接费用及机器工时计算了「全厂统一间接费用分配率」。

words.enDefinition: an overhead allocation rate calculated in advance from budgeted overhead and expected activity

examples.en: The predetermined overhead rate was set before the workshop knew its actual spending for the year.
examples.zh: 工作室还不知道全年实际花费时，就定下了「预定间接费用分配率」。

examples.en: We used the predetermined overhead rate for all jobs completed during the example month.
examples.zh: 我们对示例月份内所有完工的作业都用了「预定间接费用分配率」。

words.enDefinition: the overhead charged to jobs or output using an allocation rate

examples.en: The applied overhead on the repair job depended on how many machine hours were recorded.
examples.zh: 维修作业的「已分配间接费用」取决于记录了多少机器工时。

examples.en: We compared applied overhead with the total overhead actually incurred during the same month.
examples.zh: 我们把「已分配间接费用」与同月实际发生的间接费用总额作了比较。

collocations: compare applied overhead with actual overhead

words.enDefinition: the indirect costs that were incurred during a period, before comparing them with allocated amounts

examples.en: The accountant added rent and equipment repairs to find actual overhead for the small workshop.
examples.zh: 会计把租金和设备维修费相加，求得这间小工作室「实际发生的间接费用」。

examples.en: In the exercise, actual overhead was higher because two machines needed unexpected maintenance that month.
examples.zh: 练习中，两台机器当月需要临时维护，「实际发生的间接费用」因此更高。

collocations: compare actual overhead with applied overhead

words.enDefinition: the amount or situation when applied overhead is less than the overhead actually incurred

examples.en: We identified underapplied overhead because more indirect costs were incurred than had been charged to jobs.
examples.zh: 实际发生的间接费用多于计入各作业的金额，我们确认发生了「间接费用分配不足」。

examples.en: The underapplied overhead was shown as a debit balance in the example overhead account.
examples.zh: 示例的间接费用账户把「间接费用分配不足」显示为借方余额。

words.enDefinition: an account that records manufacturing overhead applied to production in a system that tracks actual and allocated overhead separately

examples.en: We credited the manufacturing overhead allocated account when the workshop applied overhead to unfinished jobs.
examples.zh: 车间把制造费用分配给尚未完工的作业时，我们贷记「已分配制造费用账户」。

examples.en: The tutor reconciled the balance in the manufacturing overhead allocated account with total overhead costs incurred.
examples.zh: 导师将「已分配制造费用账户」的余额与实际发生的制造费用总额核对。

collocations: credit the manufacturing overhead allocated account
reconcile the manufacturing overhead allocated account
close the manufacturing overhead allocated account

words.enDefinition: the measure, such as machine time or labour hours, used to distribute overhead

examples.en: We chose machine hours as the overhead allocation base for costs in the printing department.
examples.zh: 我们用机器工时作为印刷部门成本的「间接费用分配基础」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the overhead allocation base reflected how the two products used the workshop.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「间接费用分配基础」能不能反映两种产品对工作室的实际使用情况。

words.enDefinition: the process of charging production overhead to units using an absorption rate or other allocation basis

examples.en: The exercise showed overhead absorption into product costs before we calculated the closing inventory total.
examples.zh: 我们计算期末存货总额前，练习先展示了产品成本如何进行「间接费用吸收分配」。

examples.en: Our lecturer explained why overhead absorption could differ from the actual overhead incurred in the month.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了为什么「间接费用吸收分配」的金额可能与当月实际间接费用不同。

collocations: effect of overhead absorption on unit costs

words.enDefinition: identifying the objects that should bear costs and assigning the costs to them by tracing or allocation

examples.en: The worksheet covered cost assignment after we had collected the costs for both printing orders.
examples.zh: 我们归集了两笔印刷订单的成本后，练习表接着讲「成本归属分配」。

examples.en: A new cost assignment method charged the exhibition's equipment use to the groups that used it.
examples.zh: 新的「成本归属分配」方法把展览的设备使用成本记给用过设备的各组。

words.enDefinition: assigning a cost to the specific object it can be directly linked to

examples.en: We used cost tracing to assign the blue fabric to the order that actually used it.
examples.zh: 我们用「成本追溯归属」把蓝布成本记到了实际使用它的订单上。

examples.en: The tutor distinguished cost tracing from allocating the rent shared by all orders in the workshop.
examples.zh: 导师把「成本追溯归属」与在全部订单间分摊工作室租金区分开。

collocations: cost tracing to a specific job

words.enDefinition: anything for which a separate cost is measured, such as a product, job, service or department

examples.en: We treated each custom sign as a cost object because it used different materials and time.
examples.zh: 由于每块定制标牌的用料和工时各异，我们把每块都当作「成本对象」。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to identify the cost object before classifying any of the listed expenses.
examples.zh: 导师让我们先确定「成本对象」，再对列出的各项开支分类。

collocations: trace costs to a cost object
allocate overhead to a cost object

words.enDefinition: a unit of output, service or activity for which a cost is calculated

examples.en: The cost of a repair per bicycle used one bicycle as the cost unit in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习按每辆自行车计算修理费用，把一辆自行车定为「成本核算单位」。

examples.en: We selected an hour of support as the cost unit for the equipment desk.
examples.zh: 我们选一小时支持服务作为器材服务台的「成本核算单位」。

words.enDefinition: an income statement that deducts variable expenses from sales to show contribution margin before fixed expenses

examples.en: The variable costing income statement grouped expenses by behaviour and reported contribution margin near the middle.
examples.zh: 「变动成本法利润表」按成本性态归类费用，在中段报告边际贡献。

examples.en: We used a variable costing income statement to see how additional sales affected the contribution margin.
examples.zh: 我们用「变动成本法利润表」查看增加的销量怎样影响边际贡献。

collocations: prepare a variable costing income statement
review the variable costing income statement
compare a variable costing income statement with absorption costing

words.enDefinition: a cost centre that accumulates the cost of internal services provided to other organisational units

examples.en: The service cost centre collected the repair team's costs before assigning them to production departments.
examples.zh: 「辅助服务成本中心」先归集维修团队的成本，再分配给生产部门。

examples.en: We allocated the service cost centre costs according to the maintenance hours each department used.
examples.zh: 我们按各部门使用的维护工时分摊「辅助服务成本中心」归集的费用。

collocations: allocate a service cost centre's costs

words.enDefinition: a share of a cost assigned to a cost object according to a chosen allocation method

examples.en: The allocated cost for the weekend class included its share of the studio's monthly rent.
examples.zh: 周末课程「分摊后计入的成本」包括它应承担的那部分月租。

examples.en: We compared the allocated cost for two activities that used the same workshop on different days.
examples.zh: 我们比较了在不同日期用同一间工作室的两项活动各自「分摊后计入的成本」。

words.enDefinition: indirect costs that have not been assigned to a cost object or included in allocated costs

examples.en: The example showed unallocated overhead separately from the costs already charged to finished products.
examples.zh: 例子把「未分配的间接费用」与已经计入完工产品的成本分开列出。

examples.en: Our tutor asked why the unallocated overhead remained after the usual distribution at the end of the period.
examples.zh: 导师问，期末正常分配后为什么还有「未分配的间接费用」。

words.enDefinition: a method assigning actual direct costs to output and applying overhead using a predetermined rate

examples.en: The shop used normal costing to charge actual paper costs and apply overhead at its predetermined rate.
examples.zh: 车间采用「正常成本法」，按实际金额计入纸张成本，按预定费率分配制造费用。

examples.en: Our tutor explained how normal costing let managers estimate job costs before actual overhead was known.
examples.zh: 导师解释了管理者如何在实际间接费用尚未确定时，用「正常成本法」估算作业成本。

words.enDefinition: a method using actual direct costs and overhead assigned with an actual rate based on actual costs and activity

examples.en: The exercise used actual costing after we had final figures for materials, labour and indirect expenses.
examples.zh: 我们拿到材料、人工和间接费用的最终数字后，练习采用了「实际成本法」。

examples.en: We compared actual costing with a method that assigned overhead using the estimated annual rate.
examples.zh: 我们把「实际成本法」和一种采用预估年度费率分配间接费用的做法作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the average output expected under normal conditions over several periods, allowing for planned interruptions

examples.en: We estimated normal capacity from several years of typical output, allowing for scheduled maintenance.
examples.zh: 我们用几年的典型产量估算「正常生产能力」，并考虑了计划内维护。

examples.en: The lecturer compared normal capacity with output from an unusually quiet month in the workshop.
examples.zh: 讲师把「正常生产能力」与工作室特别清闲的一个月的产量作了比较。

collocations: allocate costs based on normal capacity

words.enDefinition: available capacity after allowing for normal breaks, maintenance and other unavoidable interruptions

examples.en: Our practical capacity estimate allowed for staff breaks and scheduled maintenance on the equipment.
examples.zh: 我们估算「实际可供使用的产能」时考虑了员工休息和设备的计划内维护。

examples.en: The exercise calculated an hourly cost from practical capacity rather than assuming uninterrupted operation.
examples.zh: 练习依据「实际可供使用的产能」计算每小时成本，不假定可以一直运转。

collocations: cost per hour of practical capacity

words.enDefinition: the maximum achievable output or available time under ideal conditions with no interruptions

examples.en: The class calculated theoretical capacity before allowing for breaks and time spent replacing materials.
examples.zh: 课堂先算「理论产能」，然后才考虑休息和更换材料要花的时间。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why theoretical capacity was greater than the amount the workshop could normally deliver.
examples.zh: 导师解释了为什么「理论产能」比工作室平时能完成的工作量更大。

collocations: compare actual output with theoretical capacity

words.enDefinition: the amount of productive capacity made available by the resources an organisation has provided

examples.en: We compared capacity supplied with the actual processing time used by the returns department last month.
examples.zh: 我们将「资源供给产能」与退货部门上个月的实际处理时间作了比较。

examples.en: Adding another shift increased capacity supplied even though demand for the service did not immediately change.
examples.zh: 尽管服务需求没有立即变化，多排一个班次增加了「资源供给产能」。

collocations: measure capacity supplied in labour hours
compare capacity supplied with capacity used

words.enDefinition: a costing method assigning resource costs to activities and then to objects based on their use of those activities

examples.en: Our shop applied activity-based costing after discovering that small orders required most of the setup work.
examples.zh: 发现小单占用了大部分准备工作后，店里采用了「作业成本法」。

examples.en: The lecturer used activity-based costing to compare products requiring different numbers of inspections before sale.
examples.zh: 讲师用「作业成本法」比较售前检查次数不同的几种产品。

words.enDefinition: a grouping of costs associated with a particular activity for subsequent allocation

examples.en: We placed checking and packing costs in separate groups, starting with the inspection activity cost pool.
examples.zh: 我们把检查和打包费用分组，先归集与检验有关的「作业成本库」。

examples.en: The activity cost pool contained expenses connected with preparing the printer for each different batch.
examples.zh: 该「作业成本库」归集了给打印机更换批次、做好准备的相关费用。

collocations: group costs in an activity cost pool
assign costs to an activity cost pool
select a driver for an activity cost pool

words.enDefinition: the cost assigned per unit of the driver used to measure an activity

examples.en: We calculated the activity rate for inspections using estimated inspection costs and the expected inspection count.
examples.zh: 我们用估算的检查成本和预计检查次数计算了检查的「作业成本分配率」。

examples.en: The worksheet applied the activity rate to the number of setups each product needed that week.
examples.zh: 练习表把「作业成本分配率」乘以当周每种产品所需的准备次数。

words.enDefinition: a measure of how much of an activity a product, service or other cost object consumes

examples.en: We chose the number of setups as the activity driver for the workshop's preparation costs.
examples.zh: 我们用设备准备次数作为工作室准备成本的「作业动因」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the activity driver reflected actual inspection effort for all the products.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「作业动因」能不能反映所有产品实际需要的检查工作量。

words.enDefinition: a measure used to assign the cost of a resource to the activities that use it

examples.en: We used floor space as the resource driver for assigning rent to several different workshop activities.
examples.zh: 我们采用占用面积作为「资源动因」，把租金分配给几项不同的工作室作业。

examples.en: The tutor distinguished a resource driver from the measure used to assign activity costs to products.
examples.zh: 导师把「资源动因」与将作业成本分配给产品时使用的衡量标准区分开。

collocations: allocate costs using a resource driver

words.zhGloss: 按作业次数计量的动因
words.enDefinition: a cost driver measuring how many times an activity is performed
acceptedZhAnswers: 按作业次数计量的动因

examples.en: The number of purchase orders was a transaction driver for the equipment office's ordering costs.
examples.zh: 采购订单数量是器材办公室订购成本的「按作业次数计量的动因」。

examples.en: We used a transaction driver because each recorded inspection took approximately the same amount of time.
examples.zh: 每次记录的检查花费时间大致一样，我们用了「按作业次数计量的动因」。

collocations: measure an activity with a transaction driver

words.zhGloss: 按作业时长计量的动因
words.enDefinition: a cost driver based on the amount of time an activity takes
acceptedZhAnswers: 按作业时长计量的动因

examples.en: We used setup hours as a duration driver because large batches took longer to prepare.
examples.zh: 较大的批次要准备更久，所以我们用准备工时作为「按作业时长计量的动因」。

examples.en: The model changed to a duration driver after the tutor showed how inspection times varied.
examples.zh: 导师演示各次检查的用时差异后，模型改用「按作业时长计量的动因」。

collocations: compare costs using a duration driver

words.zhGloss: 按实际耗用资源计量的动因
words.enDefinition: a cost driver that assigns resources based on the particular effort or resources used for an instance of an activity
acceptedZhAnswers: 按实际耗用资源计量的动因

examples.en: The exercise used an intensity driver to capture specialist staff and equipment used in unusual repairs.
examples.zh: 练习采用「按实际耗用资源计量的动因」，计入复杂维修用到的专业人员和设备。

examples.en: Our lecturer explained why an intensity driver might be more accurate but more expensive to measure.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了为什么「按实际耗用资源计量的动因」可能更准确，计量成本却更高。

collocations: measure effort with an intensity driver

words.enDefinition: assigning costs from resources to intermediate pools or activities and then to final cost objects

examples.en: The model used two-stage allocation to assign equipment costs to activities and then to custom products.
examples.zh: 模型采用「两阶段成本分配」，把设备成本先计入作业，再分配给定制产品。

examples.en: We drew arrows showing each part of the two-stage allocation in the classroom printing example.
examples.zh: 我们给课堂印刷案例画了箭头，标明「两阶段成本分配」的各个环节。

words.enDefinition: a classification of costs according to the level of activity that causes them

examples.en: The cost hierarchy placed setup costs at the batch level and assembly costs at the unit level.
examples.zh: 「成本层级」把准备成本列为批次级，把组装成本列为单位级。

examples.en: Our tutor used a cost hierarchy to explain why not all costs followed the number of units.
examples.zh: 导师用「成本层级」说明，为什么并非所有成本都随产量变动。

collocations: classify activities in a cost hierarchy

words.enDefinition: an activity performed for each individual unit of a product or service

examples.en: Attaching a strap was a unit-level activity because every bag needed one before it was sold.
examples.zh: 装背带是「单位级作业」，每个包在出售前都要装一根。

examples.en: In the workbook, labelling each notebook was classified as a unit-level activity during final preparation.
examples.zh: 练习册把最后准备时逐本给笔记本贴标签归为「单位级作业」。

words.enDefinition: an activity undertaken for a batch regardless of how many units it contains

examples.en: Changing the printing plates was a batch-level activity because we did it once for each batch.
examples.zh: 更换印版是「批次级作业」，因为每批只换一次。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether checking the batch setup counted as a batch-level activity in the case.
examples.zh: 讲师问，核查批次准备在案例中是否算「批次级作业」。

words.enDefinition: an activity supporting a particular product line regardless of the number of units or batches made

examples.en: Maintaining the booklet's design files was a product-level activity even when nothing was being printed.
examples.zh: 即使没在印刷，维护那本小册子的设计文件也是「产品级作业」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether revising the instructions for one kit was a product-level activity instead.
examples.zh: 导师问，修订一种套件的说明书是否应算「产品级作业」。

words.enDefinition: an activity performed to support a particular customer or account rather than a specific unit or batch

examples.en: A monthly planning call with the society was a customer-level activity for the print shop.
examples.zh: 每月和社团开一次筹备电话会议，对印刷店来说是「客户级作业」。

examples.en: The workbook classified managing one customer's billing arrangement as a customer-level activity in the example.
examples.zh: 练习册把案例中管理某个客户的账单安排归为「客户级作业」。

words.enDefinition: an activity supporting the whole facility rather than particular products, batches or customers

examples.en: Cleaning the common workshop floor was a facility-level activity serving all three production areas.
examples.zh: 清洁共用工作室地面是「设施级作业」，服务于三个生产区。

examples.en: We treated maintaining the building alarm as a facility-level activity in the costing exercise.
examples.zh: 成本练习里，我们把维护建筑报警系统视为「设施级作业」。

words.enDefinition: an activity-based method using the cost per time unit of available capacity and the time needed for work

examples.en: We tested time-driven activity-based costing to find how much time rush orders used at the counter.
examples.zh: 我们试用「时间驱动作业成本法」，估算加急订单用了多少柜台时间。

examples.en: Our tutor introduced time-driven activity-based costing before comparing unused capacity across two different departments.
examples.zh: 导师先介绍「时间驱动作业成本法」，再比较两个不同部门的闲置产能。

words.enDefinition: the cost of supplying a resource divided by the practical capacity it makes available

examples.en: We divided the cost of the support team by its practical hours to find the capacity cost rate.
examples.zh: 我们用支持团队的总成本除以实际可用工时，得出「单位产能成本率」。

examples.en: The capacity cost rate was expressed in pounds per available hour in the workshop example.
examples.zh: 工作室示例里的「单位产能成本率」用每可用小时多少英镑来表示。

words.enDefinition: an equation estimating how long an activity takes based on features of a transaction or job

examples.en: Our time equation added several minutes whenever the order needed its own separate packaging.
examples.zh: 订单需要单独包装时，我们的「作业耗时方程」就会多算几分钟。

examples.en: The lecturer checked whether the time equation included extra time for verifying unfamiliar account details.
examples.zh: 讲师核查「作业耗时方程」有没有计入确认陌生账户详情的额外时间。

collocations: estimate activity time with a time equation

words.enDefinition: a description of the different activities used in a costing system and how they are defined

examples.en: We recorded each stage of packing in the activity dictionary so both departments used the same terms.
examples.zh: 我们在「作业字典」记录打包各环节，让两个部门都用同一套词。

examples.en: The activity dictionary explained what counted as an inspection in the print shop's costing model.
examples.zh: 「作业字典」解释了在印刷店的成本模型里，哪些工作算一次检查。

collocations: define activities in an activity dictionary

words.enDefinition: using information about activities and their costs to manage resources and improve operations

examples.en: We used activity-based management to identify repeat inspections that added little value for customers.
examples.zh: 我们用「基于作业的管理」找出对顾客价值不大的重复检查。

examples.en: The class linked activity-based management to changes the workshop could make in its order process.
examples.zh: 课堂把「基于作业的管理」和工作室在订单流程中可作的调整联系了起来。

words.enDefinition: a misleading assignment of costs that results in inaccurate cost estimates for products, services or other objects

examples.en: The simple allocation method caused cost distortion because two products used very different setup times.
examples.zh: 两种产品所需准备时间差别很大，简单分配法造成了「成本扭曲」。

examples.en: We looked for cost distortion after seeing two identical overhead charges for very different orders.
examples.zh: 发现两笔差异很大的订单间接费用竟然一样后，我们检查是否有「成本扭曲」。

words.enDefinition: systematically undercosting some items and overcosting others because of how shared costs are assigned

examples.en: The lecturer used cost cross-subsidisation to explain how custom orders appeared cheaper than they really were.
examples.zh: 讲师用「产品间成本交叉补贴」解释，为什么定制订单看起来比实际便宜。

examples.en: The broader allocation base caused cost cross-subsidisation between standard products and the smaller specialist lines.
examples.zh: 粗放的分配基础让标准产品与量较小的专门产品之间出现了「成本交叉补贴」。

words.enDefinition: assigning the costs of internal support departments to the operating departments or other units they serve

examples.en: We used service department cost allocation to distribute equipment maintenance costs among three production areas.
examples.zh: 我们用「辅助部门成本分配」把设备维护费分摊给三个生产区。

examples.en: The tutor explained why service department cost allocation mattered when both production areas used the same support team.
examples.zh: 导师解释了两个生产区共用一个支持团队时，为什么「辅助部门成本分配」很重要。

collocations: methods of service department cost allocation

words.enDefinition: a method assigning support department costs directly to operating departments without allocating support costs among support departments

examples.en: The workbook used the direct allocation method for a simple example with two operating departments.
examples.zh: 练习册用「直接分配法」演示了一个有两个业务部门的简单例子。

examples.en: We discussed which internal services the direct allocation method left out of the calculation.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「直接分配法」没有纳入计算的内部服务有哪些。

collocations: costs under the direct allocation method

words.enDefinition: a method allocating support costs in sequence, including some services between support departments

examples.en: The step-down allocation method assigned the maintenance team's costs first because it supported several departments.
examples.zh: 「阶梯分配法」先分配维护团队的成本，因为它为多个部门提供支持。

examples.en: We compared two results from the step-down allocation method after reversing the order of allocation.
examples.zh: 我们颠倒分配顺序后，比较了「阶梯分配法」算出的两个结果。

collocations: choose the order for the step-down allocation method

words.enDefinition: a method allocating support department costs while accounting for services provided to one another

examples.en: The exercise used the reciprocal allocation method because two support departments regularly helped each other.
examples.zh: 两个辅助部门经常互相协助，练习因此使用了「交互分配法」。

examples.en: Our lecturer used simultaneous equations to demonstrate the reciprocal allocation method in the classroom example.
examples.zh: 讲师用联立方程演示了课堂案例里的「交互分配法」。

collocations: calculate costs with the reciprocal allocation method

words.enDefinition: a measure of how much support a department receives, used as a basis for assigning costs

examples.en: We used the number of repair calls as a service usage measure for allocating maintenance costs.
examples.zh: 我们用报修次数作「内部服务用量指标」，分配维护成本。

examples.en: The lecturer asked whether the service usage measure reflected the time each department actually needed.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「内部服务用量指标」能否反映各部门实际需要的服务时间。

collocations: allocate costs using a service usage measure

words.enDefinition: the order in which different groups of costs are assigned

examples.en: We changed the allocation sequence to see how it affected the cost charged to printing.
examples.zh: 我们调整了「分配顺序」，观察它如何影响计入印刷部门的成本。

examples.en: The workbook showed the allocation sequence for support departments before listing the final assigned costs.
examples.zh: 练习册先展示辅助部门的「分配顺序」，再列出最终分配的成本。

words.enDefinition: services one department provides to another within the same organisation

examples.en: We measured interdepartmental services by the hours each department spent on requests from another team.
examples.zh: 我们用各部门处理其他团队请求的工时衡量「部门间服务」。

examples.en: The case explained why some interdepartmental services were included in the cost allocation calculation.
examples.zh: 案例解释了为什么有些「部门间服务」纳入了成本分配计算。

collocations: allocate the cost of interdepartmental services

words.enDefinition: costs attached to units moved from an earlier production department into the current one

examples.en: The finishing department recorded transferred-in costs when it received partly completed notebooks from printing.
examples.zh: 后道加工部门收到印刷部门转来的半成品笔记本时，记录了「上道工序转入成本」。

examples.en: The exercise separated transferred-in costs from additional costs incurred in the current department that month.
examples.zh: 练习把「上道工序转入成本」与当月本部门新增成本分开列出。

words.enDefinition: a measure turning work done on complete and partly complete items into an equivalent number of fully complete units

examples.en: We used equivalent units to express the finishing work done on the partly completed notebooks.
examples.zh: 我们用「约当产量」表示对尚未完工笔记本已完成的后道加工工作量。

examples.en: The tutor calculated equivalent units separately for materials because they were added at the start.
examples.zh: 由于材料从一开始就投入，导师单独计算了材料的「约当产量」。

words.enDefinition: a schedule reconciling the actual units available with units completed, lost or still in process

examples.en: The physical flow schedule showed how many units remained unfinished at the end of the month.
examples.zh: 「实物数量流程表」显示月底还有多少件没做完。

examples.en: We completed the physical flow schedule before calculating equivalent units for direct materials and conversion.
examples.zh: 我们填完「实物数量流程表」后，才计算直接材料和加工的约当产量。

words.enDefinition: a process costing report summarising production quantities, equivalent units and costs assigned during a period

examples.en: The production cost report showed separate amounts for completed output and the units still in process.
examples.zh: 「生产成本报告」分别列出了完工产量和仍在加工的单位数对应的金额。

examples.en: Our instructor asked us to prepare a production cost report for the final assembly department.
examples.zh: 老师请我们给最后一道组装部门编制「生产成本报告」。

collocations: production cost report for a department

words.enDefinition: a schedule showing where the costs to be accounted for have been assigned

examples.en: The cost reconciliation schedule matched the available costs to completed output and ending work in process.
examples.zh: 「成本核对表」把待分配成本对应到完工产量和期末在产品。

examples.en: We checked the cost reconciliation schedule after rounding the cost per equivalent unit in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的单位约当成本四舍五入后，我们核对了「成本核对表」。

words.enDefinition: the opening units plus units started or transferred in that must be explained in a production schedule

examples.en: Our units to account for included the notebooks already in process at the start of April.
examples.zh: 我们的「待核对的实物数量」包括四月初已经在加工的笔记本。

examples.en: The tutor checked units to account for before reviewing what happened to the output that period.
examples.zh: 导师先查看「待核对的实物数量」，再看本期产量的去向。

collocations: compare units to account for with units accounted for

words.zhGloss: 已核对去向的实物数量
words.enDefinition: the units in a production schedule whose disposition is recorded, such as completed, lost or unfinished units
acceptedZhAnswers: 已核对去向的实物数量

examples.en: The units accounted for included completed units and those still waiting for a cover to be fitted.
examples.zh: 「已核对去向的实物数量」包括完工件和还没装上封面的件数。

examples.en: We checked that units accounted for matched the number reported as available during the period.
examples.zh: 我们核对了「已核对去向的实物数量」是否等于本期报告的可用实物总数。

words.enDefinition: the costs that must be explained in a production report, including opening work and current-period additions

examples.en: The costs to account for included the cost already attached to the opening unfinished notebooks.
examples.zh: 「待分配的成本总额」包含已计入期初在产品笔记本的成本。

examples.en: The tutor calculated costs to account for before assigning costs to the completed units.
examples.zh: 导师先算「待分配的成本总额」，再向完工品分配成本。

collocations: calculate total costs to account for

words.zhGloss: 已分配并解释去向的成本
words.enDefinition: the costs whose assignment to outputs, inventory or other destinations is recorded in a costing report
acceptedZhAnswers: 已分配并解释去向的成本

examples.en: The costs accounted for included amounts assigned to both transferred output and unfinished inventory.
examples.zh: 「已分配并解释去向的成本」包括分到转出产品及未完工存货的金额。

examples.en: After correcting the rounding, we checked that costs accounted for matched the total we started with.
examples.zh: 更正四舍五入差额后，我们核对了「已分配并解释去向的成本」是否与起初总额一致。

words.enDefinition: units whose production began and ended within the current accounting period

examples.en: Our units started and completed excluded notebooks that were partly finished before the month began.
examples.zh: 「本期投产并完工数量」不包括月初之前已做完一部分的笔记本。

examples.en: The exercise presented units started and completed on a separate line in the FIFO calculation.
examples.zh: 练习在先进先出计算中单列「本期投产并完工数量」。

words.enDefinition: units still being manufactured at the end of a period, or their recorded inventory cost

examples.en: The report valued ending work in process using the amount of work performed on unfinished units.
examples.zh: 报告按对未完工单位已完成的工作量计量「期末在产品」。

examples.en: We counted ending work in process after the workshop stopped accepting new orders for the day.
examples.zh: 工作室当天停止接新单后，我们清点了「期末在产品」。

collocations: cost assigned to ending work in process

words.enDefinition: unfinished units already in production at the start of a period, or their recorded inventory cost

examples.en: The exercise included beginning work in process from orders that were started the previous month.
examples.zh: 练习纳入了上个月已开始生产的订单中的「期初在产品」。

examples.en: We calculated how much additional work the beginning work in process needed before it was finished.
examples.zh: 我们算了「期初在产品」在完工前还需要多少加工。

collocations: cost of beginning work in process

words.enDefinition: the proportion of required work performed on units that are still in production

examples.en: We estimated the degree of completion for the notebooks that still needed their covers fitted.
examples.zh: 我们估计了那些还要装封面的笔记本的「完工程度」。

examples.en: The worksheet treated degree of completion separately for materials introduced at different stages of production.
examples.zh: 练习表对不同生产阶段投放的材料分别计算「完工程度」。

words.enDefinition: the direct labour and manufacturing overhead costs of turning materials into finished output

examples.en: The tutor assigned conversion costs separately from the paper and covers used for the notebooks.
examples.zh: 导师把「加工成本」和笔记本所用的纸张、封面成本分开分配。

examples.en: We calculated the conversion costs for the finishing department using labour and applied overhead together.
examples.zh: 我们用人工和已分配间接费用合计计算了后道加工部门的「加工成本」。

words.zhGloss: 在工序开始时投入的材料
words.enDefinition: materials introduced at the beginning of a production process rather than gradually during it
acceptedZhAnswers: 在工序开始时投入的材料

examples.en: The problem specified materials added at the start to explain why unfinished units already included paper.
examples.zh: 题目指定了「在工序开始时投入的材料」，说明未完工单位为什么已经包含纸张。

examples.en: We treated materials added at the start as fully included once an item entered the process.
examples.zh: 产品进入工序时，我们就视同「在工序开始时投入的材料」已全部计入该产品。

collocations: assume materials added at the start
costs for materials added at the start
account for materials added at the start

words.enDefinition: the amount of a cost category divided by the equivalent units assigned to that category

examples.en: We found the cost per equivalent unit for conversion before assigning any costs to unfinished output.
examples.zh: 给未完工产量分配成本之前，我们先求出了加工的「单位约当成本」。

examples.en: The lecturer compared cost per equivalent unit for materials with the amount calculated for conversion.
examples.zh: 讲师把材料的「单位约当成本」与加工部分算出的数字作了比较。

collocations: estimate the cost per equivalent unit
cost per equivalent unit for conversion

words.enDefinition: process costing that combines opening work-in-process costs with current costs when calculating equivalent-unit costs

examples.en: The worksheet used weighted-average process costing to pool the opening and current costs of materials.
examples.zh: 练习表用「加权平均分步成本法」汇总期初与当期材料成本。

examples.en: Our tutor compared weighted-average process costing with FIFO using a month with opening unfinished stock.
examples.zh: 导师用月初有未完工存货的一个月比较了「加权平均分步成本法」与先进先出法。

words.enDefinition: process costing that separates work on opening inventory from units started during the current period

examples.en: In FIFO process costing, we separated completing opening units from producing units started during the month.
examples.zh: 在「先进先出分步成本法」中，我们把完成期初在产品与生产当月投产单位分开处理。

examples.en: The lecturer showed how FIFO process costing used current costs to calculate this month's equivalent-unit cost.
examples.zh: 讲师演示了「先进先出分步成本法」如何用本期成本计算当月的单位约当成本。

words.enDefinition: spoilage expected under usual efficient operating conditions in a production process

examples.en: The workshop budget allowed for normal spoilage when several printed covers might come out unusable.
examples.zh: 工作室预算允许出现「正常废品损失」，因为可能有几张印出的封面不能用。

examples.en: We treated the small number of torn labels as normal spoilage in the classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 课堂练习中，我们把少数破损标签当作「正常废品损失」。

words.enDefinition: spoilage beyond what is normally expected under efficient production conditions

examples.en: The broken printer caused abnormal spoilage because far more covers were unusable than we usually expected.
examples.zh: 打印机故障使无法使用的封面远多于通常预计，造成了「异常废品损失」。

examples.en: The costs of abnormal spoilage were shown separately in the exercise rather than charged to ordinary output.
examples.zh: 练习把「异常废品损失」单列，没有计入正常产出。

collocations: record a loss from abnormal spoilage

words.enDefinition: the stage in production at which units are checked for defects or spoilage

examples.en: The inspection point came after printing because that was when damaged covers could be identified.
examples.zh: 「生产检验点」设在印刷后，因为这时才能发现受损的封面。

examples.en: The exercise asked which units had reached the inspection point before the month ended.
examples.zh: 练习问，在月末前哪些单位已经到达「生产检验点」。

words.enDefinition: the amount expected from selling or recovering materials left over or rejected during production

examples.en: We estimated the scrap value of the offcuts before calculating the net cost of spoiled units.
examples.zh: 我们先估了边角料的「废料残值」，再算废品的净损失。

examples.en: The worksheet recorded a small scrap value for the metal left after cutting the brackets.
examples.zh: 练习表给切完支架剩下的金属记了一笔小额「废料残值」。

words.enDefinition: a reduction in the quantity of usable output during a production process

examples.en: The example recorded process loss when some paper was trimmed away while making the notebooks.
examples.zh: 制作笔记本时裁掉了部分纸张，案例中记为「制程损耗」。

examples.en: The lecturer separated expected process loss from the much larger loss caused by the equipment fault.
examples.zh: 讲师把预期的「制程损耗」与设备故障造成的更大损失分开。

words.enDefinition: the extra usable output that occurs when actual process loss is lower than normal expected loss

examples.en: The exercise reported an abnormal gain because the batch lost fewer units than the expected amount.
examples.zh: 那一批损耗件数低于预期，练习报告了「异常增益」。

examples.en: We calculated the abnormal gain in units before explaining how it changed the department's cost report.
examples.zh: 我们先按单位数计算「异常增益」，再解释它如何改变部门成本报告。

words.enDefinition: a process that produces two or more outputs together before each can be identified separately

examples.en: The lecturer used joint production to describe how one cutting process yielded two usable materials.
examples.zh: 讲师用「联合生产」描述一个切割过程如何同时产出两种可用材料。

examples.en: We discussed whether the costs of joint production could be traced to each separate output.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「联合生产」的成本是否能追溯到每种独立产出。

words.enDefinition: the process of apportioning costs incurred before the split-off point among outputs of a joint production process

examples.en: Our example used joint cost allocation to assign the shared dairy processing costs to both outputs.
examples.zh: 示例使用「联合成本分配」把乳品共同加工成本分配给两种产出。

examples.en: We compared how two methods of joint cost allocation affected the reported cost of each product.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两种「联合成本分配」方法如何影响各产品的报告成本。

collocations: apply a joint cost allocation method
compare bases for joint cost allocation
calculate the result of joint cost allocation

words.enDefinition: the stage in a joint process at which its separate products first become individually identifiable

examples.en: At the split-off point in the dairy example, cream and skim milk became separately identifiable products.
examples.zh: 在乳品加工的例题中，奶油和脱脂奶到「分离点」时就可以作为不同产品辨认。

examples.en: The workbook asked which processing costs were incurred after the split-off point for each product.
examples.zh: 练习册问，每种产品在「分离点」之后发生了哪些加工成本。

words.enDefinition: one of multiple significant products obtained together from a single process

examples.en: The tutor treated the two saleable paper grades as joint products from one processing line.
examples.zh: 导师把一条加工线产出的两种可售纸张等级视为「联产品」。

examples.en: Each joint product had a substantial sales value in the example, unlike the leftover scraps.
examples.zh: 示例中每种「联产品」都有可观的销售价值，剩下的碎料则不同。

words.enDefinition: an output from a process with relatively minor value compared with its main products

examples.en: The worksheet treated the small wood offcuts as a by-product of making the shelves.
examples.zh: 练习表把做架子剩下的小块木料列为「副产品」。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked how revenue from the by-product would appear in the production report.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「副产品」收入会怎样显示在生产报告中。

words.enDefinition: costs incurred after the split-off point that can be traced to individual products

examples.en: We recorded polishing and packaging as separable costs because each of those tasks applied to one output.
examples.zh: 我们把抛光和包装列为「分离后可归属成本」，因为每项作业都对应单一产出。

examples.en: The worksheet deducted separable costs from the expected final sales value before allocating joint cost.
examples.zh: 练习表从预计最终销售价值中扣除「分离后可归属成本」，再分配联合成本。

collocations: assign separable costs to each product

words.enDefinition: allocating joint costs according to physical quantities such as weight, volume or units at split-off

examples.en: The physical-measure method allocated common costs using the weight of each material after the first process.
examples.zh: 「实物量分配法」用首道工序后每种材料的重量来分配共同成本。

examples.en: We tried the physical-measure method even though the outputs differed greatly in their selling prices.
examples.zh: 尽管各项产出的售价相差很大，我们还是试用了「实物量分配法」。

collocations: compare results under the physical-measure method

words.enDefinition: each joint product's total sales value at the point where it first becomes separately identifiable

examples.en: The table showed sales value at split-off before adding any amount for later painting or finishing.
examples.zh: 表格列出的是「分离点销售价值」，还没计入之后喷漆或后道加工增加的价值。

examples.en: We allocated joint costs in proportion to the sales value at split-off of each output grade.
examples.zh: 我们按各产出等级的「分离点销售价值」所占比例分配联合成本。

collocations: allocate using sales value at split-off

words.enDefinition: a joint cost allocation method using estimated final sales value less separable costs for each product

examples.en: The worksheet used the net realizable value method because neither output had an observable split-off price.
examples.zh: 两项产出都没有可观察的分离点价格，练习表用了「可变现净值分配法」。

examples.en: We compared the net realizable value method with an allocation based on the weight of each output.
examples.zh: 我们把「可变现净值分配法」与根据各项产出重量做的分配作了比较。

collocations: apply the net realizable value method
use the net realizable value method
allocate joint costs by the net realizable value method

words.enDefinition: a joint cost allocation method that assigns costs so all joint products show the same gross margin percentage

examples.en: Our lecturer used the constant gross margin method to allocate shared production costs to both outputs.
examples.zh: 讲师用「固定毛利率分配法」把共同生产成本分配给两项产出。

examples.en: We checked that the constant gross margin method produced the same percentage for each joint product.
examples.zh: 我们核实了按「固定毛利率分配法」，各项联产品的毛利率是否一样。

collocations: use the constant gross margin method
apply the constant gross margin method
allocate by the constant gross margin method

words.enDefinition: an explanation of why particular allocation bases or methods were chosen for an indirect cost

examples.en: The cost allocation rationale explained why we used floor space to distribute the shared workshop rent.
examples.zh: 「成本分配依据」说明了为什么用占用面积分摊共用工作室的租金。

examples.en: Our tutor asked for a clearer cost allocation rationale after seeing that the two departments used equipment differently.
examples.zh: 导师看到两个部门使用设备的方式不同，要求写清「成本分配依据」。

words.enDefinition: an income statement using inventory and cost of goods sold that include allocated fixed manufacturing overhead

examples.en: The absorption costing income statement included allocated fixed manufacturing costs in the cost of units sold.
examples.zh: 「完全成本法利润表」把已分配的固定制造费用计入已售单位的成本。

examples.en: We compared the absorption costing income statement with the version that showed contribution margin separately.
examples.zh: 我们把「完全成本法利润表」和单独列出边际贡献的那张表作了比较。

collocations: prepare an absorption costing income statement
review an absorption costing income statement
figures in an absorption costing income statement

words.enDefinition: a cost not arising from the production of goods, such as selling or general administration costs

examples.en: The class classified the fee for advertising the booklets as a nonmanufacturing cost in the example.
examples.zh: 课堂把示例中给小册子做广告的费用归为「非制造成本」。

examples.en: The sample report listed a nonmanufacturing cost for advertising below the cost of goods sold.
examples.zh: 示例报告在销售成本下方列了一项广告费，属于「非制造成本」。

collocations: exclude nonmanufacturing costs from product inventory

words.enDefinition: the cost assigned to one unit of product under a specified costing method

examples.en: The workbook calculated unit product cost after the workshop finished all the banners for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 工作室做完展览用的全部横幅后，练习册计算了「单位产品成本」。

examples.en: Our unit product cost changed when we allocated part of the rent to the new batch.
examples.zh: 把部分租金分给新一批产品后，我们的「单位产品成本」发生了变化。

words.enDefinition: the total production cost of goods completed during an accounting period

examples.en: The class calculated cost of goods manufactured before using finished goods balances to calculate cost of goods sold.
examples.zh: 全班先计算「完工产品成本」，再用产成品余额计算销售成本。

examples.en: We included the opening unfinished work when calculating cost of goods manufactured for the example month.
examples.zh: 计算示例月份的「完工产品成本」时，我们纳入了期初在产品。

collocations: schedule of cost of goods manufactured

words.expression: schedule of cost of goods manufactured
words.lemma: schedule of cost of goods manufactured
words.enDefinition: a statement reconciling manufacturing costs and changes in work in process to determine completed production costs
acceptedEnVariants: schedule of cost of goods manufactured

examples.en: The schedule of cost of goods manufactured showed opening unfinished work above the new production costs.
examples.zh: 「完工产品成本计算表」把期初在产品列在新增生产成本上方。

examples.en: We prepared a schedule of cost of goods manufactured before completing the example income statement.
examples.zh: 我们先编制「完工产品成本计算表」，再填完示例利润表。

collocations: prepare a schedule of cost of goods manufactured
review the schedule of cost of goods manufactured
read a schedule of cost of goods manufactured

words.enDefinition: a reconciliation from opening to closing work-in-process inventory, showing costs added and costs transferred out

examples.en: We used the work in process rollforward to explain why unfinished orders carried a higher balance.
examples.zh: 我们通过「在产品余额变动表」解释，为什么未完工订单对应的余额更高。

examples.en: The work in process rollforward showed the costs transferred to finished goods at month end.
examples.zh: 「在产品余额变动表」列出了月末转入产成品的成本。

collocations: prepare a work in process rollforward
review the work in process rollforward
reconcile a work in process rollforward

words.enDefinition: a reconciliation from opening to closing finished goods, listing transfers in and costs removed

examples.en: The finished goods rollforward showed that costs transferred in exceeded the costs of items sold in May.
examples.zh: 「产成品余额变动表」显示，五月转入的产成品成本超过已售产品的成本。

examples.en: We checked the finished goods rollforward against the monthly closing inventory report for the workshop.
examples.zh: 我们把「产成品余额变动表」与工作室的月末库存报告作了核对。

words.enDefinition: a reconciliation of opening raw materials, additions, materials issued and ending raw material inventory

examples.en: The raw materials rollforward showed that the workshop issued more paper than it purchased in April.
examples.zh: 「原材料余额变动表」显示，四月工作室领用的纸超过购入量。

examples.en: I compared the raw materials rollforward with the records from the store before preparing my report.
examples.zh: 我先把「原材料余额变动表」与库房记录比对，再编制报告。

words.enDefinition: the cost of providing one defined unit of a service, such as a repair or an hour of support

examples.en: We calculated the service unit cost of one hour at the student equipment repair desk.
examples.zh: 我们计算了学生器材维修台每小时的「单位服务成本」。

examples.en: The tutor asked which items were included in the service unit cost for each delivery.
examples.zh: 导师问，每次送货的「单位服务成本」纳入了哪些项目。

words.enDefinition: assigning a shared cost to units according to the floorspace used by each of them

examples.en: The workshop used floor-space allocation to divide the rent between printing and equipment storage.
examples.zh: 工作室按「占用面积分摊」租金，分别计入印刷区和器材储存区。

examples.en: The class questioned whether floor-space allocation was appropriate for electricity used by specialised equipment.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了专用设备的电费是否适合「按占用面积分摊」。

words.enDefinition: an accounting entry moving assigned costs from one account, department or stage of production to another

examples.en: We posted a cost transfer entry when the completed notebooks moved to the finished goods account.
examples.zh: 完工笔记本转入产成品账户时，我们做了一笔「成本转移分录」。

examples.en: The lecturer explained how the cost transfer entry moved accumulated costs from one process to another.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了「成本转移分录」怎样把归集的成本从一道工序转入另一道工序。

words.enDefinition: the full-unit equivalent of processing labour and overhead applied to the units being measured

examples.en: We calculated equivalent units for conversion separately because workers finished the notebooks in several stages.
examples.zh: 工人分几个阶段做完笔记本，我们单独计算了「加工约当产量」。

examples.en: The equivalent units for conversion were fewer than the units counted as complete for materials.
examples.zh: 「加工约当产量」少于就材料投入而言已完成的单位数。

collocations: divide conversion cost by equivalent units for conversion

words.enDefinition: the full-unit equivalent of direct materials already added to the units being measured

examples.en: Our equivalent units for materials included every unit that had received its full share of paper.
examples.zh: 「直接材料约当产量」包括已经投入所需全量纸张的每件产品。

examples.en: The worksheet reported equivalent units for materials separately from the figures for processing and assembly.
examples.zh: 练习表把「直接材料约当产量」与加工、组装部分的数字分开列出。

collocations: divide material costs by equivalent units for materials

words.enDefinition: an activity that contributes value to the product or service in the eyes of the customer

examples.en: The class identified repairing a loose handle as a value-added activity when servicing a borrowed bicycle.
examples.zh: 课堂把维修借来的自行车时拧紧松动把手归为「增值作业」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether printing a personalised name counted as a value-added activity for the workshop.
examples.zh: 导师问，对工作室而言，印上顾客定制的姓名算不算「增值作业」。

words.enDefinition: an activity that uses resources without increasing the value of the output for its customer

examples.en: The workshop identified moving the same box twice as a non-value-added activity in its process.
examples.zh: 工作室把流程里同一箱子搬两遍视为「不增值作业」。

examples.en: We discussed whether the non-value-added activity was still necessary because of the way records were kept.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了，考虑到现在的记录方式，那项「不增值作业」是否仍然必需。

words.enDefinition: assigning a shared cost in proportion to quantities such as the number of units or transactions

examples.en: The retail team used quantity-based allocation to divide sorting costs among the three types of kits.
examples.zh: 零售团队采用「按数量分摊」的办法，在三种套件之间分配分拣费用。

examples.en: We compared quantity-based allocation with an approach based on how long each repair took to finish.
examples.zh: 我们把「按数量分摊」与按各次维修所耗时间进行的分配作了比较。

words.enDefinition: assigning costs in proportion to the machine time recorded for each product, job or department

examples.en: We used machine-hour allocation because the larger signs needed significantly more time on the printer.
examples.zh: 印大标牌占用设备的时间长得多，所以我们用了「按机器工时分配」。

examples.en: The lecturer compared machine-hour allocation with allocation based on the number of posters in each order.
examples.zh: 讲师把「按机器工时分配」和按各单海报数量分配作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the process of choosing a measure that reasonably reflects what causes a particular cost to change

examples.en: The tutor treated cost-driver selection as a separate step before we calculated any allocation rates.
examples.zh: 导师把「成本动因选择」列为一个单独步骤，完成后才算各项分配率。

examples.en: We revisited cost-driver selection when the number of orders no longer reflected the inspection work needed.
examples.zh: 订单数不再能反映必要的检查工作量时，我们重新作了「成本动因选择」。

words.enDefinition: a check that costs collected in a pool agree with source records and assigned or remaining balances

examples.en: Our cost pool reconciliation found a printing charge that had been included twice in the worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们的「成本库核对」发现，有一笔印刷费用在工作表里计了两次。

examples.en: The lecturer requested a cost pool reconciliation before comparing the amounts allocated to each product.
examples.zh: 讲师要求先做「成本库核对」，再比较分配给各项产品的金额。

words.enDefinition: the cost of an activity or department that enables other organisational work

examples.en: We included a support cost for maintaining the booking system used by both workshop areas.
examples.zh: 我们计入了一笔「支持职能成本」，用于维护两个工作区都用的预约系统。

examples.en: The tutor asked why a support cost had been assigned entirely to one production department.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么一笔「支持职能成本」完全计入了一个生产部门。

words.enDefinition: a count of units that are still being produced at the time of checking

examples.en: The in-process inventory count found twelve notebooks waiting for their covers at the end of term.
examples.zh: 学期末「在产品盘点」发现，有十二本笔记本还没装封面。

examples.en: We carried out the in-process inventory count before recording completion percentages for each batch of products.
examples.zh: 我们先做了「在产品盘点」，再记录各批产品的完工百分比。
